change: Include fixed-address memory-returned call fields in the loop-carried frame inventory, with disjoint ABI-width ranges.
scope: Proof coverage and emitted-code selection only. No runtime or compilation timing was measured. The stronger plain-body verdict currently retains more checks; this is not a performance improvement.
reproduce: Use base_commit for before. For after, apply this commit relative to its parent, restricted to production_files, onto base_commit.
Build each emitter with: go build -o EMITTER ./benchmarks/native/emit
env OAK_NATIVE_ONLY=hash__blake3_uupdate OAK_VERIFY_CACHE=0 OAK_VERIFY_BUDGET= OAK_NATIVE_DUMP=1 OAK_OPT_REPORT=1 EMITTER benchmarks/kernels/oak PREFIX > PREFIX.stdout 2> PREFIX.log
The changed loop summary does not modify the native lowering or admission policy. Search prefers a witness-checked body over a trusted body.

after.selection: analysis  search             73 candidate(s) considered, 73 lowered, 3 verified; selected identity (witnessed, cost 1312595.0; identity 1312595.0)
after.verdict: native backend: asm unit hash__blake3_uupdate: agrees with its Oak body on 305 concrete inputs (evidence, not proof: one iteration of loop 3 was not proven to preserve next.cv[0] = next.cv[0] + (state.cv[0] sub loop1.next.cv[0]) (a valuation refutes it, as every other pairing of next.cv[0]))
after.cache: native backend: 0 of 3 verdicts from the verdict cache

remaining_limits: The plain BLAKE3 update body reaches 305 concrete inputs, but the inductive coupling of next.cv[0] in nested call events is not proved.
Guard-elided forms still lose .stack_len after an indexed store forgets part of the result area.
Constant aggregate result leaves have a separate loop-coupling limitation. The reduced loop fixtures use changing leaves.

Calls whose result address cannot be reconstructed within one basic block or from a loop-invariant frame base remain outside this form. RV64 memory-returned calls and union results remain unsupported.
